the on-strip digestion procedure described in this paper can be used to minimize the diffusion of peptides after trypsin digestion and can be used for identification of proteins separated by IEF on IPG strips.

trypsin digestion can be carried out on the IPG strip, which is a simple, rapid and effective method for protein identification by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, and that post-digest ion diffusion is reduced significantly using this method.
we developed a spray-based method for on-strip digestion of proteins embedded within IPG strips.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method of protein digestion that is compatible with IPG strips and can be easily implemented in a routine proteomics lab.
the development of a new method to improve MALDI-TOF MS analysis of IPG-separated protein samples, and the results are promising for further applications of IPG-based proteomics.
the development of novel sample preparation techniques that can be used to improve the performance of MALDI-TOF MS analysis of IPG-separated protein samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spray method is an effective and simple method for the digestion of proteins embedded on IPG strips for MALDI-TOF mass spectral analysis.

the on-strip digestion of proteins embedded into an IPG matrix using this procedure can lead to a significant improvement in peptide recovery and identification, and thus the identification of proteins separated by IEF.
the use of this approach for the digestion of proteins on IPG strips is highly recommended for subsequent MALDI-TOF MS analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this approach is useful in the analysis of proteins on IPG strips by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, and also to perform 'on strip' trypsin proteolysis.
'on-strip' digestion of proteins in IPG strips can be effectively performed by using the spray procedure.
'on-strip' tryptic digestion of proteins on IPG strips is an excellent approach to identify proteins in the 2D map.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a small amount of trypsin (0.2 microg/strip) and a short incubation time (10 min) are critical in minimizing the diffusion of tryptic peptide ions from the IPG strip.

this procedure allows the analysis of intact proteins and tryptic peptides on the same spot on the IPG strip, thereby allowing a direct comparison of the two sets of data, leading to the identification of proteins.
trypsin digestion can be performed on intact IPG strips to obtain high quality MALDI-TOF mass spectra of the tryptic peptides.
